77892.subject: Weekly Recap: Washington's Rally
77892.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

Bitcoin gained 22.6% this week, its largest weekly move since Trump won the 2024 elections.

The trigger came out of Washington's debt management office. The **Treasury** said it would at least double its buybacks of long-dated debt, lifting the maximum operation size in the 10-to-30-year sectors to $4 billion. The 30-year yield fell to 5.21% from Monday's close, and about $3 billion of liquidations followed the break, more than 90% of them shorts.

Washington supplied the rest. **Trump** pressed the Senate to pass the Clarity Act, with cloture on H.R. 3633 ripening Sept. 15, and said CFTC Chair Michael Selig is working to bring **Hyperliquid** onshore, a venue that geoblocks Americans while clearing $6.19 billion of perps a day. The **SEC** proposed a token-offering framework that lets an issuer certify its way out of securities law.

**Stripe** agreed to pay more than $7 billion for AI gateway **OpenRouter**, a company that reached 200 trillion monthly tokens without touching the stablecoin issuer, the wallets or the settlement chain Stripe already owns.

Enjoy!

## How Maple Finance Became the #2 Crypto Lender Behind Tether

Youtube: How Maple Finance Became the #2 Crypto Lender Behind Tether — Sid Powell Explains (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xR4dp43CSSo)

Sid Powell walks through the Robinhood Earn plumbing behind Maple's roughly $4.6 billion in assets, with deposits routed through a Morpho vault curated by Steakhouse into syrupUSDG, plus DAO-only governance, the token buyback and why he thinks the competition is Blackstone and Ares.

———————————————————————————

# Top Stories This Week

## Bitcoin Posts Its Biggest Week Since the 2024 Election

Bitcoin traded at $76,977 on Friday, up 6.4% in a day and [22.6% over seven days](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-reaches-79-500-as-2-75-billion-liquidation-claim-lacks-detail), its largest weekly gain since the week to Nov. 12, 2024. The move broke a $59,000-to-$67,000 range that had held for seven weeks. Ether added 28.8%, XRP 36.7% and Solana 21.5%. US spot bitcoin ETFs took in $606.3 million on Thursday, $503 million of it into BlackRock's IBIT. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index read 72, against 29 a week earlier.

## Trump Says the CFTC Is Working to Onshore Hyperliquid

Trump said Wednesday that CFTC Chair Michael Selig is working to bring Hyperliquid into the US “in a fully compliant and legal fashion,” speaking beside SEC Chair Paul Atkins, ICE's Jeffrey Sprecher and Coinbase's Brian Armstrong. The exchange [geoblocks US and Ontario users](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/trump-says-cftc-working-to-onshore-hyperliquid) while clearing $6.19 billion of perps volume over 24 hours and holding $11.72 billion of open interest. HYPE rose about 19% to $69.56. CME Group and Cboe closed down 1.7% and 3.5%.

It now seems possible to vaccinate against cancer


Tim Cross

Senior science writer


Over the past decade or so the four stalwarts of cancer treatment—surgery, radiation, chemotherapy and targeted drugs—have been joined by a fifth. As its name suggests, immunotherapy aims to prod the body’s immune system into destroying cancerous cells. These days, drugs designed to bolster a patient’s immune response are used against dozens of different kinds of cancer.


One promise of immunotherapy, though, has remained mostly unfulfilled. For decades scientists have tried, and generally failed, to develop cancer vaccines. That lacklustre record is one reason for the excitement that surrounded the announcement on August 19th by Moderna, an American drug firm,
